editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — October 8, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: openclaw/openclaw is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: openclaw/openclaw leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: openclaw/openclaw — 77 commits today, 443.9 below its current daily pace, with 96 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
NousResearch/hermes-agent — 20 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
unslothai/unsloth — No same-day commit after 534 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Give screenshot judgments a separate test in Pi
dailyInsight.insight: Pi 1.1.0 adds images and OpenAI Decisions to its existing classifier interface. Agent scripts can ask a bounded visual question and receive a typed result they can use in subsequent code.
dailyInsight.mechanism: Codemode forwards an image block and JSON task state through models.classify. The OpenAI adapter serializes the image with the state and returns a Boolean probability, choice or score; a refused answer produces an error result rather than automatic fallback.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: Builders can isolate recurring screenshot questions from the main chat and compare that path with their current review method. The callable interface makes the comparison possible; its accuracy still needs measurement.

actions.audience: Builders already using Pi scripts for interface review
actions.label: Prepare a small labeled screenshot comparison
actions.instruction: Use non-sensitive screenshots with known defects and unchanged question criteria. Compare classifier and chat outputs for missed defects and false alarms before giving either authority to approve a change. Record latency and all billed work when you choose to run the experiment.
actions.effort: One small test-set preparation and optional API trial

receipts.title: Image input and OpenAI Decisions adapter
receipts.supports: Adds classifier image context, provider mapping and typed script support.

receipts.title: Pi 1.1.0 containing release
receipts.supports: Published October 8 in Paris; downloaded npm packages contain the compiled support.

receipts.title: Screenshot classification example
receipts.supports: Shows the intended image-plus-task request and bounded layout question.

confidence.basis: Pinned implementation and mocked test definitions inspected; containing npm artifacts downloaded and checked against registry hashes.

dailyInsight.limitation: No live API call, package execution or visual-accuracy test was performed. OpenAI API-key access is required; a ChatGPT OAuth sign-in does not make this classifier available in Pi. Returned probabilities are not calibration evidence.
dailyInsight.falsifier: A reproducible containing-release test showing images are dropped or the typed result cannot reach codemode would overturn the interface finding; a labeled evaluation showing no useful accuracy/cost tradeoff would weaken the proposed use.
dailyInsight.watchNext: A fixed screenshot set with identical criteria, expected defects, missed-defect and false-alarm rates, latency and complete billed work for classifier versus chat.
